statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 82%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ trades at 29,411.50, down 0.13%, and is in a fourth consecutive hour inside the unchanged 29,364.00-29,508.25 overnight band. Both edges of that band have produced retracements: the 29,508.25 high was rejected three hours ago and never retested, and the 29,364.00 low has held. That is mean-reverting behaviour rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions. VIX at 16.48 is unchanged on the day inside a 16.29-16.52 range, and the 2-year at 4.45% has moved half a basis point. Stress is held one point higher at extreme because the energy leg has extended again: Brent is $102.18, up 0.96% and the highest since May, WTI is $97.47, up 1.48%, and the 10-year has printed 4.86%, its highest since 2023, while roughly 56-60% odds are priced for a 25 basis point increase on 16 September. Producer prices are due at 12:30 UTC and consumer prices tomorrow. A narrow danger window is published around the producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open rather than a broad session-wide restriction.
headline: NQ holds 29,411.50 inside an unchanged 29,364.00-29,508.25 overnight band for a fourth hour with VIX flat at 16.48, while Brent extending to $102.18 and a 10-year at 4.86% keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC producer price release
body:
Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,411.50, down 37.25 points or 0.13% against a 29,448.75 prior settle, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,508.25 after opening at 29,458.50. That 144.25-point band, roughly 0.49% wide, is now unchanged for a fourth consecutive hour. The 29,508.25 high was set three hours ago, rejected immediately and never retested; the 29,364.00 low has held and price sits roughly 48 points above it. Both extremes have therefore produced retracements and the intervening path has been a fade rather than an extension, which is mean-reverting behaviour and not the persistent directional efficiency that defines tail conditions. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 86.15 points or 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range and beneath a 29,507.70 prior close.

Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive and the energy leg has extended further. Brent trades at $102.18, up 0.96%, its highest since May, and WTI is $97.47, up 1.48%. The driver is the continuing exchange of strikes between US and Iranian forces on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz, alongside Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities including the Jazan refinery, which forced temporary operational halts. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.86%, up about two basis points and its highest since 2023, while the 2-year at 4.45% is up half a basis point. That bear-steepening pattern is a term-premium and inflation-expectation move rather than a front-end repricing, and it leaves the curve spread near 41 basis points. VIX at 16.48 is unchanged on the day in a 16.29-16.52 range, so options are not pricing a tail event.

Internal participation is dispersed rather than aligned. The semiconductor index closed 9 September up 1.30% at 11,887.87 while the Nasdaq-100 fell 0.29%, and megacap performance in the latest session ranged from a large gain in one name to losses of more than one and a half percent in others. Dispersion of that kind works against index-level directional efficiency, because it means the index is being pulled in both directions rather than carried by a single aligned bloc. That is the main reason Tail stays in the low band despite an unambiguous stress regime.

The scheduled sequence is dense. Producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims are due at 12:30 UTC, existing home sales at 14:00 UTC, consumer prices at 12:30 UTC tomorrow, and the FOMC decision with projections on 16 September at 18:00 UTC, where roughly 56-60% odds are priced for a 25 basis point increase from the current 3.50-3.75% range. Consistent with the published risk definitions, event importance and forecast dispersion raise Stress and reduce Confidence in the later horizon rather than raising Tail before a print is observed. The published conditional path therefore lifts Tail into the WATCH band only for the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, where a release and the cash open overlap, and no slot on the horizon reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 08:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 8% to 20% and has held a tight 8-11% band throughout the overnight session as retracements kept appearing at both ends of the range. Stress climbed from 79% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set successive cycle highs, then settled at 80-81% for the last eight hours. Confidence held between 87% and 89% throughout. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail between 10% and 11% through the remaining European session, lifts it to 20% in the 12:00 UTC release hour and a horizon peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing would overlap the US cash open, then decays it to 12-19% across the US afternoon and to a 9-13% overnight band into the consumer price session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout because Brent above $100, a 10-year at its highest since 2023 and roughly even odds of a September rate increase are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 66% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.

VIX 16.48 is flat. Stress stays extreme because Brent has extended to $102.18 and the 10-year has printed 4.86%, its highest since 2023.

forecast.analysis: European mid-morning. The published path assumes the overnight band continues to contain price; a sustained break of 29,508.25 or 29,364.00 that is not retraced within the hour would be the first structural change, and is the checkpoint this slot is scored against.
drivers: Checkpoint: whether 29,508.25 or 29,364.00 gives way without a retracement
European cash session liquidity typically widens the band before the US release

A first spike is normally two-sided; only a second leg that extends without retracement would be genuine tail behaviour, and none can be observed yet.
drivers: US PPI, Core PPI and initial jobless claims at 12:30 UTC
Release mechanics, not observed structure, drive the WATCH mapping here

forecast.analysis: Horizon peak. Post-release repricing would overlap the 13:30 UTC cash open, the one window where an opening auction can extend a release move. Scored conditionally: shallow pullbacks plus a hold near the session extreme would be the amplifier, and it remains unobserved.
drivers: Post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30 UTC US cash open
Conditional amplifier: shallow pullbacks plus a hold near a session extreme
Opening auction is the historical route from a release into one-way structure
Rate-hike odds near 60% make a firm print a live repricing catalyst

forecast.analysis: Existing home sales at 14:00 UTC is a secondary print. Tail decays back below the WATCH band on the assumption that opening-hour price discovery is orderly and retracements reappear; a failure of that assumption would keep the higher scores of the prior slot in force.
drivers: US existing home sales at 14:00 UTC as a secondary checkpoint
Assumption: orderly opening-hour discovery with retracements returning
Invalidation: repeated extension after failed pullbacks would hold Tail higher

forecast.analysis: US late morning. Post-release volatility usually decays into this window and the published path assumes cross-assets stabilise. Stress stays extreme independently of the release because oil above $100 and a cycle-high long end are regime features a single data point does not clear.
drivers: Assumed post-release volatility decay through US late morning
Stress is regime-driven: Brent above $100 and a 10-year near cycle highs
Checkpoint: whether yields hold their advance after the release

Semis and megacaps have been diverging rather than moving as one bloc

Assumption: orderly close with the day's repricing complete

drivers: Post-close futures session, historically the quietest window
Thin liquidity raises gap sensitivity, not sustained trend probability

drivers: No scheduled catalysts in this window
Assumption: US-session range carries into the Asian handover

drivers: Asian session opening with the low end of the overnight Tail band
